sentences.text: 1 This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 02.03.2024 at about 6.10 a.m, the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-R-7681 from Vykunta Bar circle towards Gangondanahalli on the extreme left side of Madanayakanahalli road, in slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached Opposite to Mohan Medical Store,
Dasanapura Hobli, Benglauru, at that time suddenly the rider of Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-EU-0173 drove the same in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed against to SCCH-23 the petitioner's motorcycle.

As a result of which he sustained grievous injuries and after the accident he was shifted to Prakriya Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone several surgeries and was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.

It is specifically urged that he was working as Junior Machinist/ Operator at Steer Engineering Pvt. Ltd and earning Rs.55,313/- p.m. and due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the scooter.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and rider of the Honda Activa scooter and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Despite due service of the notice of the petition upon them, the respondents failed to appear before this Tribunal.
Hence they were placed exparte.
SCCH-23 4.
The petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to P14 were marked on his behalf.
5. Arguments were addressed by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.
6. The following points are raised for consideration :

POINTS 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 02.03.2024 at about 6.10 a.m., Opposite Mohan Medical Store, on Madanayakanahalli road, Dasanapura Bengaluru, due to actionable negligence of the rider of Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-EU-0173 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
7.

My answers to the above points are as follows :-

2  Point No.1 : In the Affirmative  Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Point No.3 : As per final order  for the following :
8. POINT NO.1:

sentences.text: The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the rider SCCH-23 of Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03-EU-0173 for the offences punishable u/s's 279 & 338 of IPC and u/s 181, 196 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
In spite of due service of the notice of petition upon them, the respondents No.1 & 2 failed to appear before this Tribunal.
Hence they were placed exparte.
Thus the evidence led by the petitioner has remained unchallenged.

Consequently, based on the material available on record, I hold that actionable negligence on the part of the rider of Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-03- EU-0173 in causing the accident in question is proved.
Therefore, I answer point No.1 as 'In the Affirmative.
9. POINT NO.2 :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : 1)
Head injury- right fronto - Temporal contusion, 2) multiple facial fractures and 3) Right 3rd Metacarpal fracture.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Ex.P11 Discharge Summary discloses that the petitioner was taken treatment at Prakriya Hospitals from 02.03.2024 to 13.03.2024 for a period of (11 SCCH-23 days).

During the course of treatment he underwent surgeries in the form of : ORIF-Zygomatic complex fracture + Orbital floor exploration +
Floor Reconstruction, CRIF with K wire- 3 rd Metacarpal neck fracture.

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
10. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :

The petitioner has deposed that he was working as Junior Machinist/ Operator at Steer Engineering Pvt. Ltd and earning Rs.55,313/- p.m. and due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
In order to prove the said fact he has produced 3- Pay slips at Ex.P.13.
Except this the petitioner has not produced the appointment letter, Bank statement or any other documents before this Court.
Further he has also not examined the author of ExP.13.
However he has neither proved his avocation nor his earning capacity.
However he has neither examined the doctor nor produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the SCCH-23 petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
Though PW.1 deposed in his evidence affidavit that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to continue avocation.
So also no iota of evidence is placed on record to show that he has sustained loss of income during treatment period.
Non- production of the any documents in this regard results in drawing of an inference that he has not suffered any financial loss during the period of his treatment.

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
11. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 11 days is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would Dileep Kumar M vs Basha on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85050615/
3 have accompanied her to the hospital to take him care by leaving their duties.

sentences.text:
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and SCCH-23 nutrition.

Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index,
the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.13,200/- (1,200 X 11) is awarded under this head.
12. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
13. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P9, the petitioner has spent Rs.5,43,197/-
towards medical expenses.
All these bills have been examined with care and are found to be correct.
Moreover he has not been cross examined by the respondents.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.11- Duplicate copy of Discharge summary, wherein the current sponsor name is mentioned as The Oriental Insurance Company Limited.

On perusal of SL.No.60 of Ex.P.9 being the Credit Final Bill,
wherein it is clearly mentioned the total bill amount is Rs.5,26,739.46, in that amount hospital authorities have given discount of Rs.81,739.01.

After discount the total amount will comes to Rs.4,45,000/-, in that amount the insurance company SCCH-23 approved and credit limit of Rs.2,00,000/- and the total payable amount is mentioned as Rs.2,45,000/-.
Hence the petitioner has paid Rs.2,45,000/- to the hospital.
On perusal of Sl.No.1 to 5 of Ex.P.9, they are advance bills.
Sl.No.6 to 43, 45 to 56, 58 pharmacy bills amount are already included in the IP bill.
The Sl.No.44 for a sum of Rs.210/- and Sl.No.57, for a sum of Rs.1,354/- are purchased from other medical shops.
Hence the petitioner is entitled (Rs.210 + Rs.1,354 + Rs.2,45,000) for Rs.2,46,564/- which is rounded off to Rs.2,46,600/- towards medical expenses.

14. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
15. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred SCCH-23 therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

16. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Loss of future income due to : - Nil - disability 2 Loss of income during laid-up : -
Nil - period 3 Attendant charges, extra : 13,200-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 4 Pain & sufferings : 50,000-00 5 Medical expenses : 2,46,600-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : 40,000-00 happiness 7 Future medical expenses : - Nil - Total 3,49,800-00 Dileep Kumar M vs Basha on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85050615/
4 17.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
18. The respondent No.1 is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
He has not produced any document to show that his vehicle had insurance coverage at the time of accident.
It is well settled that a person driving a vehicle is presumed to have authority to do the same unless the contrary is proved.

In SCCH-23 the absence of any contrary evidence in this regard and also considering the fact that the claimant has established that the accident was caused by the rider of the offending vehicle (respondent No.2 herein), the respondent No.1 is vicariously liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Tribunal.
Hence he is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
19. POINT NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,49,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.
SCCH-23 After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
